stories.title: Russia says it's ready to restart three-way peace talks as its missiles hit Kyiv
stories.summary: After meeting US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in St Petersburg, the [[kremlin|Kremlin]] said it could resume talks with the US and Ukraine in mid-November. Overnight, Russian strikes on Kyiv injured six people. Zelenskyy says Ukraine's early-warning system for missile attacks is working again after talks with US officials.
stories.background: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The last US-mediated talks were in February 2026, just before the US and Israel went to war with Iran, and the effort stalled after that. The new plan is a meeting of negotiators from all three countries about security guarantees once the fighting stops. Kyiv worries the Trump administration is moving closer to Moscow, and US envoy Witkoff drew criticism from both parties after calling Putin a 'humanitarian'.

sources.title: Russian missiles hit Kyiv as Moscow signals readiness for peace talks
What happened during Witkoff and Kushner's latest meeting with Putin
Kremlin says 'ready' to resume 3-way talks with US and Ukraine mid-November
Zelenskyy says early warning system for Russian missile attacks resumes

stories.title: Houthi attacks force Saudi Arabia to cancel its flagship investor summit
stories.summary: An attack on King Fahd International Airport killed one person and injured eight. The US ordered some staff to leave the kingdom, Saudi Arabia called off its '[[fii|Davos in the Desert]]' conference, and Macron flew to Riyadh unannounced to show support.
stories.background: Yemen's [[houthis|Houthis]] are aligned with Iran and fought a Saudi-led coalition for years before that war wound down. Since the US–Israeli war on Iran began in February 2026, Iran and its allies have struck targets around the Gulf, and Al Jazeera describes the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as a new front in that wider conflict. The US had already pulled staff out of the region once, early in the war.

sources.title: One killed, eight injured in attack on Saudi Arabia's King Fahd airport
US orders departure of personnel from Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi threat
Macron visits Riyadh to show solidarity amid Houthi attacks
Saudi Arabia cancels 'Davos in the Desert' due to Yemen's Houthi strikes

stories.title: Paris bans protests after days of unrest, and France's borrowing costs jump
stories.summary: Police banned demonstrations in parts of Paris after the violent riots of 17 October. French [[bond-yield|bond yields]] went above 5%, the highest since 2002. Marine Le Pen is rising in the polls, an NGO says pro-Russian accounts amplified the anger online, and Macron rejected Trump's claim that migrants caused the riots.
stories.background: The protests began over the cost of living and rising fuel prices, led by high school students and the [[yellow-vests|Yellow Vests]] movement. When they turned violent, the government imposed nightly curfews in Paris and other big cities. Investors now want more to lend to France, which makes its debt more expensive at a tense political moment, with Le Pen preparing to launch her presidential campaign.

sources.title: Live: Paris bans protests after violent unrest as Macron takes swipe at Trump
French bond yields hit 24-year high after unrest
In run-up to mass protests and riots, pro-Russian accounts amplified French anger, NGO finds
Le Pen sees polls boost amid mass protests, riots

stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their defence doctrine is now 'offensive'
stories.summary: The [[irgc|IRGC]] threatened to invade any country that attacks Iran. Separately, the leaders of Qatar and France called for the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] to reopen to shipping and for the Gaza ceasefire to be put into effect.
stories.background: The US and Israel went to war with Iran in February 2026. A US–Iran understanding in June was followed by renewed strikes in July, when Iran said it had closed the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar is mediating talks to reopen it, and Iran's foreign minister says Iran is willing to give diplomacy another chance.

sources.title: Iran war live: IRGC vows invasion as defence doctrine turns 'offensive'
Qatar, France call for opening of Hormuz and Gaza ceasefire implementation

stories.title: Putin frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard at Trump's request
stories.summary: The 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan had spent four years in Russian custody. His release was announced as the latest talks on ending the war in Ukraine began.
stories.background: Hubbard was arrested in Russia in 2022, accused of being a Ukrainian mercenary, and sentenced to more than six years in prison. Moscow called his release a goodwill gesture during Witkoff's visit.

sources.title: Putin releases American Stephen Hubbard from Russian prison
Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard after 4 years behind bars

stories.title: UN report: the world is on track for about 2.6°C of warming this century
stories.summary: Current national pledges fall far short of the [[paris-agreement|Paris Agreement]]'s 1.5°C goal, the [[unep|UN Environment Programme]] says, ahead of the [[cop31|COP31]] climate summit in Turkey next month. A UN report also finds a major rise in US climate pollution.
stories.background: Under the Paris Agreement, each country sets its own pledge to cut emissions, and the UN checks every year whether those pledges add up to the goal. Scientists say every tenth of a degree of extra warming brings more extreme heat, floods and sea level rise. COP31 is where countries are expected to answer this gap.

sources.title: World set to breach 1.5°C warming limit set by Paris Climate Agreement
DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises

stories.title: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case, linked to the DR Congo outbreak
stories.summary: Health officials say the case matches the [[ebola-bundibugyo|Bundibugyo strain]] behind the deadly outbreak in DR Congo. The patient had travelled from Uganda, and officials are tracing 44 contacts, mostly health workers.
stories.background: DR Congo's outbreak began in mid-May and has recorded more than 9,000 cases and over 4,000 deaths, its deadliest on record. Uganda and Kenya have also had cases. There's no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain. Nigeria contained an earlier Ebola case in 2014, during the West African epidemic that killed more than 11,000 people.

sources.title: Nigeria's first Ebola case matches DR Congo strain, health officials say
Sudan's war escalates as UN warns of wider regional crisis

stories.title: A drone strike on a market in Abyei reportedly kills at least 153 people
stories.summary: Local authorities blame Sudan's army for the strike on the Amiet market in [[abyei|Abyei]]. The UN warns that Sudan's war risks turning into a wider regional crisis, and an analyst told France 24 that neither the army nor the [[rsf|RSF]] shows any regard for civilian lives.
stories.background: Sudan's army and the RSF were once allies, but they went to war in April 2023 in a power struggle over the country's future. Abyei sits on the border with South Sudan, so a strike there raises the risk of the war pulling in neighbouring countries.

sources.title: 'Neither the Sudanese military, nor the RSF take any acknowledgement of human life in this war'
Sudan's war escalates as UN warns of wider regional crisis

stories.title: About 130 million names have been struck off India's voter rolls
stories.summary: A nationwide [[sir|revision of the voter rolls]] has set off a political crisis. NPR calls it the largest disenfranchisement in history.
stories.background: The Election Commission says the revision removes duplicate, dead and relocated voters. Opposition parties say eligible voters, often poor or from minority communities, are losing the right to vote because they can't produce the documents required. Some of the figures are draft counts and may change after appeals.

sources.title: Millions are struck off India's voter rolls in largest disenfranchisement in history

stories.title: The US accuses Canada of interfering in the midterm elections
stories.summary: Washington points to Canadian tariffs, political meetings and anti-Trump advertising ahead of the [[midterms|midterms]]. Separately, officials say a Justice Department list of likely noncitizen voters in California is unreliable.
stories.background: Relations between the two neighbours have been strained by a trade war with tariffs on both sides. Election interference usually means covert action by a foreign government. The US complaint is about Canada's public trade measures and advertising.

sources.title: US accuses Canada of election interference ahead of midterms
DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises

stories.title: A Bush brother backs the Democrat in Texas's Senate race
stories.summary: Neil Bush says he voted for James Talarico because of doubts about Republican Ken Paxton. In South Carolina, Trump is campaigning for Senator Darline Graham as her race against Democrat Annie Andrews tightens.
stories.background: Texas hasn't elected a Democrat to the US Senate since the 1980s, so a competitive race there is unusual. These Senate contests help decide which party controls the chamber after the [[midterms|midterms]].

sources.title: George W Bush's brother backs Democrat James Talarico in Texas Senate race
Trump heads to South Carolina to boost Senator Darline Graham in race

stories.title: The Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to let it build a wall at Big Bend
stories.summary: A federal judge halted the border barrier. Officials now want the Supreme Court to let construction go ahead.
stories.background: Big Bend is a remote stretch of the Rio Grande in West Texas, home to a national park with steep canyons that have long been seen as a natural barrier. Asking the Supreme Court for emergency permission is a common move when a lower court blocks a government policy.

sources.title: Trump administration seeks Supreme Court approval to build Big Bend wall

stories.title: Israel releases dozens of Americans detained in the West Bank
stories.summary: They included Brad Lander, a Democratic nominee for Congress, along with rabbis and activists who were helping Palestinian farmers with the olive harvest in the [[west-bank|West Bank]].
stories.background: The autumn olive harvest is central to many Palestinian families' income. In recent years, activists have joined farmers in the groves to deter attacks by Israeli settlers, which have increased during the harvest.

sources.title: Israel frees dozens of Americans, including U.S. Congress nominee, after West Bank detention

stories.title: AIPAC stops endorsing candidates and giving directly to campaigns
stories.summary: The pro-Israel lobbying group's affiliated [[super-pac|super PAC]] will keep spending.
stories.background: AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, is one of the most influential lobbying groups in Washington. It began endorsing candidates and giving money directly in the 2022 election cycle, after decades of not doing so.

sources.title: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates

stories.title: Mexico charges a prosecutor with treason over a drug raid involving US agents
stories.summary: US agents took part in the April operation, raising questions about whether Mexican law was followed.
stories.background: Mexican law strictly limits what foreign agents can do in the country, and US involvement in security operations has long been politically sensitive. Pressure from Washington to act against drug cartels has made the question more pressing.

sources.title: Mexico charges prosecutor with treason over US involvement in drug raid

stories.title: Daily life returns to Tigray's capital, under the shadow of a wider war
stories.summary: Residents of Mekelle, capital of [[tigray|Tigray]], are going back to their routines, but the reopening brings limited relief amid unrest and economic strain.
stories.background: Tigray was devastated by the 2020–2022 war with Ethiopia's federal government. The Pretoria peace deal ended the fighting, but tensions inside Tigray and between Ethiopia and neighbouring Eritrea have kept fears of new conflict alive.

sources.title: Tigray resumes daily life amid fears of wider war

stories.title: Why the FDLR militia's anti-Tutsi ideology has lasted so long
stories.summary: Former members of the [[fdlr|FDLR]] describe how hostility toward Tutsis took hold in the group and persisted.
stories.background: About 800,000 people, most of them Tutsi, were killed in Rwanda's 1994 genocide. Many of the killers fled into what is now DR Congo, and the FDLR grew out of them. Rwanda points to the group to explain its involvement in eastern Congo, one of the region's longest-running conflicts.

sources.title: What is the FDLR, and why does its anti-Tutsi ideology endure?

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV needs no more cancer treatment, his doctors say
stories.summary: Tests showed the cancer was localized. Surgery last week removed the lower lobe of the 71-year-old pope's right lung.
stories.background: Leo XIV, born Robert Prevost in Chicago, became the first American pope when he was elected in May 2025.

sources.title: Pope Leo needs no further treatment after cancer surgery, doctors say
Pope Leo XIV needs no further lung cancer treatment, Vatican says

stories.title: Ireland drops the need for UN approval before sending peacekeepers abroad
stories.summary: Lawmakers narrowly passed the bill. Critics say it weakens Ireland's neutrality.
stories.background: Until now, Ireland's [[triple-lock|triple lock]] meant a UN mandate was needed for larger deployments. Supporters of the change say one veto in the UN Security Council could block Irish peacekeeping missions.

sources.title: Ireland votes to end UN approval requirement for overseas peacekeeping missions

stories.title: EU prosecutors search the offices of the far-right Patriots for Europe group
stories.summary: The searches of [[patriots-for-europe|Patriots for Europe]] offices in Brussels and Strasbourg are part of a corruption inquiry into the group's defunct predecessor.
stories.background: The European Public Prosecutor's Office investigates crimes against the EU's budget. The European Parliament sits in both Brussels and Strasbourg, so its political groups have offices in both cities.

sources.title: EU prosecutors search European Parliament offices of far-right group

stories.title: Colombia's president removes museum artworks he says promote 'communism'
stories.summary: The far-right president says the National Museum is the first target of a wider campaign against cultural institutions.
stories.background: The National Museum of Colombia in Bogotá is one of the oldest museums in the Americas. Its collection covers the country's history, including its long internal armed conflict, which makes it a target in political fights over how that history is told.

sources.title: Colombian president purges National Museum of works promoting 'communism'

stories.title: Meta is ordered to pay $25bn over Facebook privacy
stories.summary: A New Mexico judge set the fines after a jury found Meta misled users about who could access their data, in a case linked to [[cambridge-analytica|Cambridge Analytica]]. Meta says the penalty restricts speech.
stories.background: US states can sue companies under their own consumer protection laws, separately from federal regulators. In 2019 Meta paid a record $5 billion to the US Federal Trade Commission over the same scandal.

sources.title: Judge orders Meta to pay $25bn in fines for Facebook privacy violations
Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal

stories.title: AI helps researchers find two security flaws in PHP
stories.summary: [[php|PHP]] runs a large share of the world's websites, and governments are warning about the weaknesses.
stories.background: A flaw in a language as widespread as PHP can affect millions of sites at once, so the usual fix is to update PHP to a patched version as soon as one is released. AI tools are increasingly used to hunt for bugs like these, by defenders and attackers alike.

sources.title: World leaders warn of security flaws found in PHP programming language

stories.title: Chatbot company Character.AI files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: It entered [[chapter-11|Chapter 11]] after legal challenges and the loss of key staff. NPR asks whether it's a warning sign for AI startups.
stories.background: Character.AI let people chat with custom AI characters and drew millions of users. In 2024 Google hired its founders and licensed its technology, a kind of deal that has let big tech companies take talent from startups without buying them outright.

sources.title: An AI chatbot files for bankruptcy. Is it a bad omen for the industry?
What this bankruptcy says about AI startups

stories.title: TikTok staff warned about child safety, and executives didn't act, court records show
stories.summary: Previously unreported court documents show employees raising alarms. One executive said leaders underestimated the harm.
stories.background: TikTok and other social media companies face lawsuits from US states and families claiming their apps harm children. Internal documents that surface in these cases often become key evidence.

sources.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act

stories.title: Boeing's 737 Max 10 is cleared for airlines to fly
stories.summary: The FAA certified the largest [[737-max|737 Max]] jet, nearly a decade after Boeing unveiled it.
stories.background: Certification was delayed by safety reviews after the 737 Max crashes and further scrutiny of Boeing's manufacturing. Airlines that ordered the Max 10 have been waiting years to fly it.

sources.title: FAA clears the way for airlines to put Boeing's long-delayed 737 Max 10 into service

stories.title: Netflix reports earnings after a leadership shake-up and more than 1,000 layoffs
stories.summary: The quarterly results come as the company works through a management overhaul.
stories.background: Quarterly earnings reports show investors how much a company earned and how many subscribers it gained. Netflix has been adding ads and live events as it looks for new ways to grow.

sources.title: Netflix holds quarterly earnings call following leadership shakeup and layoffs

stories.title: A publisher drops a prize-nominated novelist for using AI
stories.summary: Boréal cut ties with Haitian-Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien after finding AI was used to write his acclaimed debut novel.
stories.background: Publishers and literary prizes are still writing rules for AI. Many contracts now require authors to say whether AI was used, and some prizes exclude AI-written work.

Canadian publisher drops author Orelien after confirming he used AI in debut novel
